name: Join an ally's crew
summary: A soldier boards a teammate's vehicle, not as cargo and not to bring a weapon, but as extra crew. While he rides, the vehicle is lifted to a higher level: in the source unit to the top veterancy rank, with the toughness, damage, rate of fire and self-repair that go with it. He gives up his own gun and his other abilities for the ride, only one such rider counts per vehicle, and if the vehicle is destroyed he is thrown clear alive and fights on. The boost is as large as a rank earned over a whole life, but it is on loan: it sits in one hull, it shows, and it leaves with him. The levers: what the boost is, whether it ends when he steps out, how long boarding takes, what he can still do from inside, and how he fares when the hull dies.
counterplay: Focus the boosted vehicle: its badge shows which hull carries the rider, and destroying it ends the boost and leaves him on foot among your guns.
Catch him on the way: he has to reach the vehicle on foot and climb in, and he is a soldier until he does.
Be ready when the hull dies: he comes out alive but exposed, so keep anti-infantry fire on the wreck before he reaches the next vehicle.
Use the vehicle's usual counter: the boost raises its numbers, not what it can hit or resist.
Play the numbers elsewhere: two players are tied up in one hull, so the enemy is a gun short somewhere else.

other_examples.note: A one-way version. When a ranked American vehicle is destroyed, an unarmed pilot is left standing in the wreckage, or parachutes from an aircraft, carrying that vehicle's rank. Sent into another combat vehicle of any side, he adds his rank to whatever it has, up to the top rank, and becomes part of its crew: a ranked American vehicle gives up one pilot when it dies however many were sent in, and other sides' vehicles give up none. He can't be trained and can't enter a vehicle that is already at the top rank; in a transport that never ranks he just rides. On foot he is more fragile than basic infantry.

sources.title: Pilot, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: The page quotes the Generals manual on the pilot keeping his vehicle's rank and passing it to a new one.

other_examples.note: The hero soldiers can pull enemy crews out of vehicles, and they can also climb into the player's own. A vehicle with a Spartan at the controls gets better stats and can earn more veterancy, only one Spartan fits in a vehicle, and when it is destroyed the Spartan steps out unhurt. The same page says the heroes of Halo Wars 2 behave almost the same way.

The same idea with a squad as the host: a single commander figure is attached to an infantry squad, which then holds its morale better and recovers health faster for as long as he is with it. He can also shoot one of his own men to make the infantry around him fight harder.

sources.title: Dark Crusade/Commissar, Dawn of War Wiki
sources.note: The page's description field repeats the in-game unit description.

shooter_analogues.note: A player-controlled support who jumps onto an allied champion and rides along. While attached she can't be targeted by anything except towers and shots already in flight, uses her own abilities from the host's position with extra effects, and can hop to another ally or off again. She is cut loose when the host dies or goes back to base, and being pinned locks her out of attaching for a few seconds. The enemy always sees her when they see the host.

sources.title: Template:Data Yuumi/W (You and Me!), League of Legends Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: A pilot on foot can climb onto a teammate's Titan and stay there. In the first game this stops enemy pilots from climbing on and covers the rider with the Titan's shields, though the view and the aim from up there are poor. In the second game a rider who carries a Battery plugs it in, which recharges the Titan's shield, adds to its Core meter and heals it a little.

player_translation.summary: An officer on foot walks up to a teammate's vehicle and presses one key to join its crew. While they ride, the vehicle wears a top-rank badge: it is tougher, hits harder and mends itself. The rider can't shoot; they watch, ping and decide when to step out. If the hull is destroyed they are thrown clear, hurt but alive.
as_user: Your best weapon is somebody else's vehicle: you pick the teammate and the hull that will make the most of a top rank, and the moment to commit to it.
Climbing in takes a moment next to the hull. Once inside, your own gun and your other ability are locked, and you get a look-out camera and pings instead.
You can step out whenever you like, for example to boost the infantry with your other call, but boarding again has to wait for a cooldown.
When the hull dies you land beside the wreck with part of your health gone: run for the next vehicle or fight on with your sidearm.
Alone, with no teammate's vehicle near, the key does nothing, so you fall back on your gun and your other ability.
as_target: A boosted vehicle shows a top-rank badge and an officer icon on its nameplate, so you know which hull is carrying a rider.
It is the same vehicle with the same counters, only more of it, and it repairs itself, so chip damage won't hold: commit to a burst with teammates or back off.
When it blows up, watch the wreck: the rider tumbles out alive and hurt, and will head for the next hull if you let them.
Before boarding, the rider is a lone soldier crossing open ground toward a vehicle.
teammates: A built-in two-player unit: the driver fights, the officer boosts and spots, and both share credit for what the vehicle destroys.
The officer chooses whom to back, so drivers ask for it with a ping ('officer wanted') and the team steers the boost to the hull holding the line.
Only one rider counts per vehicle, so a second officer has to find a second hull: two officers make two strong vehicles, not one unbeatable one.
The driver can refuse: the seat lock and the evict key work on a rider like on any passenger.
The enemy team calls out the badge, focuses the boosted hull together, and keeps someone on anti-infantry duty for the moment it dies.
controls: Q, one counted key: next to a teammate's vehicle it starts a short climb-in, even when every normal seat is full, because the rider squeezes in as extra crew.
Aboard: the mouse moves a look-out camera around the vehicle, left mouse pings or marks what is under the cursor, and Q or E steps out. The cooldown starts when the rider leaves or is thrown out.
The universal keys still work: hold X bails out at once, and the driver's G evicts.
Out of the vehicle, the rider's own weapon and abilities work as usual.
feedback: The vehicle shows rank chevrons and the rider's icon on its nameplate, and flies a small pennant in the team colour that reads from above.
Boarding plays a short climb-in animation and a call that nearby enemies hear.
The driver's HUD lists what the rider adds; the rider's HUD shows the hull's health, the driver's name and the cooldown.
When the hull dies the rider is flung out along a visible arc and staggers for a moment, and the kill feed says the rider got away.
A hull that already has a rider shows a filled officer slot, so a second officer doesn't walk over for nothing.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS the officer is a switch inside the tank. A player needs something to do while aboard (a camera, pings, the choice of when to leave), or nobody will ride.
The source lifts the vehicle straight to the top rank. Two players in one hull should be worth about two units, so the lift may need to be smaller, or scale down for the heaviest hulls.
The source throws the officer clear alive and says nothing of his health; here he lands hurt, in line with the proposal that players are thrown out of a dying vehicle hurt, so the kill still pays.
The pages don't say whether he can leave by himself or whether the rank stays once he has left. Here he can always leave, and the boost fades a few seconds after he does.
Consent is needed in both directions: the rider can always get out, and the driver can lock the seat or evict.
A cooldown between rides stops the boost from hopping from hull to hull within one fight.

team_play.notes: Who rides inside boosts the unit: the pattern only works with a teammate's vehicle, and it makes that hull tougher and self-mending for as long as the rider stays. The enemy answers with focus fire on the badge and a second player ready for the rider.

notes: Assumes the seat system that crewed vehicles and passengers need anyway: enter, leave, bail out, evict.
The boost is a set of stat changes on the vehicle while a rider with this pattern is aboard, plus a badge.
Being thrown clear is the normal rule for anyone inside a dying vehicle.
The rider's camera and pings are the same as a passenger's.
Edge cases: a second rider, a vehicle already at top rank, a hull that is hijacked, disabled or changes form with the rider inside, and the rider leaving mid-fight.
Two players in one hull must beat two separate units or nobody rides, yet a top-rank heavy vehicle can run away with a fight; one rider per hull and a lift that scales with tier keep it bounded.
The rider is safe inside and survives the wreck, so the risk is low for a large effect; landing hurt and a long cooldown before the next ride are the price.
It rewards pairs who play together and does little for a player without a willing driver, so the unit needs a second ability that works alone.
One badge and one icon tell the whole story.
How much stronger the hull is can't be seen, so the lift should be the same on every vehicle type.
The rider being thrown clear must be loud and visible, or the wreck looks finished when it is not.

variants.name: Rank on loan
variants.summary: The rider boards a teammate's vehicle and lifts it to the top rank while aboard; one rider per vehicle, and the rider is thrown clear alive if it dies.

variants.name: Join a squad
variants.summary: The host is a teammate's infantry squad instead of a vehicle: the leader walks with it, steadies it and speeds its healing while attached.

variants.name: Hero at the controls
variants.summary: While the rider is aboard, the vehicle can also earn more rank than it could without them, so a long ride leaves it better than it was.
variants.seen_in: Halo Wars Spartans in friendly vehicles

variants.name: Carry a rank over
variants.summary: The rider brings the ranks of a vehicle lost earlier and hands them to the next hull for good, on top of the ranks it already has; the gift can be made once.

adds_strengths.why: Saves the ranks of a lost vehicle and gives them to a teammate's hull for the rest of its life.

adds_weaknesses.why: Has one gift to give, and must carry it on foot, unarmed, across the field to deliver it.

variants.name: Ride on the outside
variants.summary: The rider clings to the outside of a teammate's walker: its shields cover them, no enemy can climb on while they are there, and a carried power cell can be plugged in to recharge the host.

variants.name: Untouchable passenger
variants.summary: The rider attaches to any ally, can't be targeted while attached, uses their own abilities from the host's position and can hop from host to host; being pinned keeps them from attaching for a few seconds, and losing the host throws them off.

adds_strengths.why: Can't be shot at while riding an ally, and keeps using its own abilities from the host's position.

adds_weaknesses.why: Fragile and slow by itself, and stranded among enemies the moment its host dies.

adds_strengths.why: Turns one teammate's vehicle into a top-rank one for as long as it rides, and gets away alive if the hull is lost.

adds_weaknesses.why: Worth little without a teammate's vehicle to board, gives up its own weapon while riding, and has to cross open ground on foot to reach a hull.

countered_by.why: Destroying the boosted vehicle ends the boost and drops the rider on foot, hurt, in front of the guns.
Catches the rider on the walk to a hull, or as it is thrown clear of a wreck.

open_questions: Does the boost end when the rider leaves? The pages read are silent. (Recommended: yes, a few seconds after.)
What may the rider do while aboard: only look and ping, or also one crew action such as a short burst of faster reloading?
Does the rider need a free seat, or squeeze in as extra crew when the seats are full? (Recommended: extra crew, one per vehicle.)
How big may the lift be on a top-tier hull: the full top rank, as in the source, or one step?
If Shamble Frontlines has no ranks at all (see the open question in earn-veterancy), the boost becomes a fixed 'officer aboard' bonus. Is that still wanted?

Why this is not a twist of passenger-sets-weapon: that pattern sits on the vehicle's card and changes its weapon or job, while this one sits on the rider's card, works on any teammate's vehicle and changes only its strength. Is the split right for the generator?

shooter_fit.reason: A two-player combo built on the seat system the game needs anyway, and one badge makes it readable. Riding without a weapon is dull unless the rider gets a spotting job, and a top-rank heavy hull needs a bounded lift.
